fields.title: Batch job-claim audit and workflow writes

data.text: Implemented three batch side-effect statements in the existing claim transaction: one guarded workflow update and two INSERT SELECT writes from the already locked queue rows. Candidate/resource acquisition, leasing and commit error handling are unchanged. No public API or schema change; ADR-010 review finds no new consumer-controlled state transition or coordination obligation. Regenerated the three checked-query metadata entries with the repository SQLx 0.9.0 refresh tool against disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 and retained unrelated cache entries. Focused claim_batch_writes suite passed all 3 tests: four claim variants, 16/single/empty statement counts, audit identity and metadata, resource fences, workflow status/first-start guards and full rollback after each injected batch failure. Full scripts/verify.sh now running on pinned Rust 1.98.1.

Focused post-implementation measurement completed on Linux x86_64 / PostgreSQL 18.6. A temporary psycopg 3.3.6 probe executed old SQL from HEAD checked-query metadata and new SQL from generated metadata over a TCP delay proxy. Fixture: 16 claimed jobs, 8 workflow-linked; three warmup pairs then 12 alternating samples per version; timed only side effects, after leasing and before rollback. pg_stat_statements observed 48 versus 3 statements and exactly 40 row writes in both (8 workflow + 16 attempts + 16 events). Added RTT 0/2/5 ms gave calibrated SELECT 1 medians 0.31/2.60/5.41 ms and old/new medians 20.53/4.34, 132.06/16.51, 294.97/36.20 ms. This is a bounded SQL-phase probe, not end-to-end worker throughput or SQLx-driver evidence. Command: uv run --no-project --with psycopg[binary] python /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/measure.py; local raw results /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/measurement.json. Durable statement-count regression also observes the actual Rust public claim paths. No repository dependencies or migrations changed.

Final verification PASSED: bash scripts/verify.sh exited 0 on pinned Rust 1.98.1, Linux x86_64. It ran formatting, file budgets, all four Clippy configurations, all six matrix parts (workspace, no-default-features, doctests, consumers, runlimit, scripts), rustdoc and all five HTTP smoke profiles. Workspace test part passed in 428.681 seconds; copied-source Runledger and single-facade consumer checks also passed. Focused claim_batch_writes tests passed all 3 cases before the full run. Final git diff --check passed; Cargo.lock, migrations and public signatures remain unchanged, and canonical/postgres/runtime SQLx metadata agree. No semantic tests were relaxed, no local MSRV run, and no code commit or publication performed. Full verification log is /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/verify.log; focused log is /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/claim-tests.log. The disposable metadata/measurement PostgreSQL container was removed. Implementation, regression tests, native contract/changelog, status row, testing evidence and primary references are complete.

data.text:
Direct first-principles and adversarial review: PR 54
Reviewed commit: e453a379b26180992d7c82ab81ac7c867bfad73c
Date: 2026-10-14
Environment: Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.1, PostgreSQL 18.6, SQLx 0.9.0.

Conclusion: no confirmed correctness defect in the batched claim implementation.
Keep the current design. Physical audit rows remain proportional to the number
of claims, but sequential side-effect statements are constant at three for a
nonempty batch. Atomicity comes from the existing transaction, independently
of batching. The public claim APIs and persisted contracts are unchanged.

The candidate query takes FOR UPDATE locks before leasing; those locks remain
through both INSERT SELECT operations and commit. Queue rows supply run, attempt
and stage directly. One UUID list selects the returned claimed rows, avoiding
paired metadata arrays. Candidate resource acquisition and later lease-identity
fences remain unchanged. A unique workflow_steps.job_id keeps the linkage one
step per job; cancellation takes job locks before workflow locks. Workflow
transitions retain the ENQUEUED/RUNNING predicate, first start and output reset.
The queue helper owns audit writes and the existing workflow helper owns its
transition. Combining all writes into a larger SQL expression would add
coordination complexity without being needed for the requested batching.

Executed controls and ablations against the same three integration tests:
- Unchanged control: 3/3 passed before and after all mutations. These tests cover
  all four claim APIs, mixed direct/workflow jobs, both origins, varied identities,
  resource ownership, 16/1/0-job claims, and failures after each batch statement.
- Restore original per-job implementation: only statement-count test fails;
  16 statements per side-effect table (48 total), expected one each (3 total).
  Workflow preservation and rollback still pass.
- Remove workflow status fence: guarded-row snapshot fails.
- Remove workflow claimed-ID fence: unclaimed ninth step becomes RUNNING.
- Suppress attempt rows: per-job audit comparison finds no attempt.
- Suppress LEASED event rows: per-job audit comparison finds no lease event.
- Replace attempt identity with 1: audit records attempt 1 instead of claimed 2.
- Commit leasing before side effects: fault snapshot finds retained leases and
  resource claims. Timestamp assertions also fail.
- Reset first started_at: preserved-field count is 2 instead of 4.
- Retain old workflow output: cleared-output count is 0 instead of 4.
- Remove audit claimed-ID fences: 17 attempts/events appear instead of 16.

All ten mutations compiled and failed the intended behavioral assertions.
Compiler failures were not counted as detected regressions. Tests were not
edited. Each mutation was restored immediately; the final worktree is clean.
SQLx checked changed SQL against the disposable database (SQLX_OFFLINE=false),
without editing committed caches, migrations or Cargo.lock.

Additional tests with the restored code and committed offline metadata:
- job_execution_resources: 12/12 passed, including 100 competing claimers,
  mixed batches and filtered claimers contending for resources in opposite order.
- queue_lease_validation: 3/3 passed, including ordered writes and event failure.
- workflow_cancel_lock_order: 17/17 passed, including cancellation, continuation,
  completion, and dependent-release races.

Scope: this is direct code review and executed fault testing, not an independent
multi-model review. Ten selected mutations establish sensitivity to those faults,
not exhaustive proof over arbitrary interleavings or administrator schema changes.
No production workload or real network benchmark was added during this review.
The previously passed full verification run remains applicable to the unchanged
commit. GitHub reports all seven PR checks successful for this same commit.

Artifacts: run.py, results.json, each numbered .patch/.log, restoration.json,
neighbor-results.json and the two neighbor suite logs in this directory.
Primary locking reference rechecked:
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/explicit-locking.html#LOCKING-ROWS
INSERT reference:
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-insert.html

Confirmed on master 3b0381e (2026-10-15), user optimization point 4; follows the read-only audit batter-q9vr.

runlimit/runlimit-memory/src/attempts.rs:107 clones AttemptPolicy before looking up the subject or deciding a denial. Its PolicyId and ScopeId are Box<str> identifiers (runlimit-core/src/identifier.rs:69), so existing subjects, busy/backoff denials and capacity denials pay for two unnecessary identifier clones. The entry at attempts.rs:137 is eagerly constructed. cleanup at :240-259 collects up to 16 copied 64-byte keys into a Vec while holding the state mutex.

Borrow the policy during admission and clone it only for a genuinely vacant entry. Replace cleanup's heap vector with fixed-capacity scratch storage, retaining the 16-entry bound and cursor advancement/wrap behavior. Keep this a contained optimization of the current store.

Preserve the hard storage bound, monotonic authoritative time, active-lease protection, quiet expiry/backoff, store-bound receipt identity, generation exhaustion, stale completion behavior, and observer calls after unlocking. Existing behavioral coverage is in runlimit/runlimit-memory/tests/attempts.rs.

Confirmed mechanism on master 3b0381e (2026-10-15), user optimization point 6; follows the read-only audit batter-q9vr. Performance impact has not been measured by this investigation.

crates/batter-core/src/telemetry/metrics/keys.rs:53-58 registers every counter/histogram observation with the current recorder, including established series. Its cache stores keys, deliberately not recorder handles. In crates/batter-otlp/src/pipeline/guard.rs, registration (:224-255) enters the shared gate mutex (:108-115), validates the key and reads the shared key registry (:123-154), delegates upstream, then reacquires the gate mutex on InFlight drop (:57-64).

Profile the complete observation path under concurrent warm-series workloads, separating guard/gate/registry cost from upstream bridge/SDK aggregation. Compare one thread with increasing thread counts, the same series versus distinct admitted series, counters and histograms, and cold registration separately. Assess recorder-local caching or a cheaper admission gate only against measured bottlenecks.

Preserve scoped/local recorder selection, catalog validation before bridge allocation, full-key capacity, rejection evidence, poison behavior, and the close/delegation barrier. Existing guard_closure.rs tests require close to reject later calls, wait for active delegation, and retain rejection evidence completed during closure. Existing external handles are not revocable; do not broaden that guarantee. A process-global core handle cache would violate recorder selection.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Provide a reproducible release benchmark/profile with environment, warmup, concurrency, throughput/latency and attribution to the relevant locks. Record an evidence-backed decision to retain the design or make a bounded optimization; do not equate the existence of mutexes with a demonstrated bottleneck. Any retained change must improve the measured workload and preserve scoped-recorder routing, bounded admission, post-close rejection, waiting for in-flight delegation, and final rejection accounting under deterministic race tests. Record relevant validation; run scripts/verify.sh if implementation changes.

fields.description:
Confirmed on master 3b0381e (2026-10-15), user optimization point 7; follows the read-only audit batter-q9vr.

crates/batter-at-rest/src/crypto.rs:199 sends the fixed 32-byte data key through encrypt_bytes, whose Zeroizing<Vec> allocation is at :320, then converts the 48-byte ciphertext/tag to an array. unwrap_data_key at :219 calls decrypt_bytes, whose ciphertext.to_vec() is at :341, then copies the plaintext into Zeroizing<[u8; 32]> at :228-229.

Use fixed zeroizing scratch buffers and the existing detached-tag AES-GCM operations for these fixed-size key paths. Keep variable-size payload processing separate. Preserve zeroization on success and every error path, V1 byte encoding/tag placement, HKDF inputs, wrapper and payload AAD, authentication failure behavior, and randomness call order/count. Same-key rewrap must authenticate and return the exact header without randomness; changed-key rewrap must use a fresh wrapping nonce and leave the payload body untouched.

This removes temporary data-key buffers, not all allocations in seal/open/rewrap: AAD/HKDF buffers and key-ID/output ownership remain. Existing deterministic independent Node fixture, tamper/substitution tests and rewrap/randomness controls live in crypto/tests.rs and tests/fixtures/.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate the eliminated temporary key-buffer allocations with setup excluded and report remaining allocation counts for seal, open, same-key rewrap and changed-key rewrap. Compare release timings for empty/small payloads and rewrap without promising an unmeasured speedup. Existing V1 fixture bytes, deterministic randomness consumption, authentication/tamper rejection and rewrap contracts must pass unchanged. Keep public API and persisted format unchanged; update relevant status/contract evidence and record pinned-toolchain scripts/verify.sh results. Do not run local MSRV verification unless separately requested.

Existing-entry and denied admissions therefore clone identifiers unnecessarily. The eager or_insert value also constructs an unused Entry for an occupied key. cleanup at attempts.rs:238 collects up to 16 copied keys into a Vec while holding the state mutex.

data.text: Decision (2026-10-15, implementation session at base 3b0381ef): acceptance criterion 4's before/after allocation counts are measured with a throwaway counting-allocator probe kept outside the repository (release and debug profiles, setup and subject derivation excluded) and recorded here and in the status row as measured evidence, not as a retained test. Reason: runlimit-memory sets unsafe_code = forbid for every target, and a #[global_allocator] needs unsafe impl GlobalAlloc; no allocation-counting dev-dependency is added to the workspace. Precedent: the docs/status.md row for batter-3dl6 records throwaway-probe measurements. Committed coverage is behavioral: a new regression in runlimit/runlimit-memory/tests/attempts.rs exercises the 16-key scan bound, cursor progression and wrap across a 20-entry store with live leases, alongside the existing lifecycle tests.

Implementation evidence (2026-10-15, Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.1, base 3b0381ef). Code: runlimit/runlimit-memory/src/attempts.rs admit() borrows subject.policy() and clones it only inside or_insert_with for a vacant entry; cleanup() copies at most CLEANUP_SCAN=16 keys into a [Key; 16] stack array (zip-bounded range scan from the cursor, Unbounded when None) instead of collecting a Vec; cursor = last examined key or None. Test: cleanup_examines_sixteen_keys_per_admission_then_resumes_and_wraps in tests/attempts.rs (20-entry store, 16 held leases sorting before 4 completed failures; two busy re-admissions wrap the cursor; at t=1000 the wrapped 16-key scan sees only live leases so a full store denies StorageCapacity although four entries are reclaimable; the resumed scan reclaims all four and admits; live lease still Busy). It passes against the base source and the new source and FAILS (StorageCapacity assertion, line 337) with the bound widened to 32. Allocation probe (throwaway, outside repo, counting GlobalAlloc, identifiers 37/53 bytes, 64-byte keys, counts per single admit/complete call, setup excluded; identical in release and debug): S1 new subject/empty store: before [37,53,2480] 3 allocs, after [37,53,2480] 3 allocs (2480 = BTreeMap node, unavoidable). S2 busy denial (1 entry): before [37,53,64] 3, after 0. S4 backoff denial: before [37,53] 2, after 0. S5 existing-entry reuse (admitted): before [37,53,64] 3, after 0. S7 new subject into 1-entry store: before [37,53,64] 3, after [37,53] 2. S8 storage-capacity denial: before [37,53,64] 3, after 0. S9.1-9.4 busy denials in a 20-entry store across four consecutive cursor positions: before 2/3/3/2 allocs with cleanup Vec sizes 0/1024/256/0 bytes, after 0 in every round. S10-S12 new subjects in a 20-21 entry store: before [37,53,1024]/[37,53,256]/[37,53] , after [37,53] each. complete(Failure/Success): 0 before and after. Policy clones (37+53 bytes) remain only for a genuinely new subject; scratch allocation is gone in every case; map-node allocation is unchanged. No latency measurement was made and none is inferred. Verification: bash scripts/verify.sh completed with exit 0 at 10:29 CEST (fmt, file budget, four Clippy configurations, six test-matrix parts, rustdoc, HTTP smokes); runlimit-memory tests 9+4 pass; negative control above. data.text: Decision (2026-10-15, implementation session at base abd898766e593381c9ad3afff685224814687fdb): before/after allocation counts and release timings for seal, open, same-key rewrap and changed-key rewrap are measured with a throwaway counting-allocator probe kept outside the repository (release profile, setup excluded) and recorded here, in the docs/status.md row and in the commit message as measured evidence, not as a retained test. Reason: crates/batter-at-rest sets unsafe_code = forbid for every target, so a #[global_allocator] cannot live in its tests, and the crate guide requires its Cargo.toml to stay explicit and standalone, so no allocation-counting dependency is added. Precedent: the same decision on batter-5618 (2026-10-15). Committed coverage is behavioral: unit tests of the fixed-size wrap/unwrap primitives against the variable-size primitives and tamper rejection, plus the existing Node fixture, tamper/substitution and rewrap/randomness tests.

Implementation evidence (2026-10-15, Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.1, base abd898766e593381c9ad3afff685224814687fdb). Code: crates/batter-at-rest/src/crypto.rs wrap_data_key now calls encrypt_data_key, which copies the 32-byte key into a Zeroizing<[u8; 48]> stack scratch, encrypts in place with encrypt_in_place_detached and writes the detached tag into the trailing 16 bytes; unwrap_data_key calls decrypt_data_key, which copies the 32 ciphertext bytes into the returned Zeroizing<[u8; 32]> and authenticates/decrypts in place with decrypt_in_place_detached. Scratch is owned only by Zeroizing, so success and every error path zeroize. encrypt_bytes/decrypt_bytes keep the variable-size payload path; only a shared cipher() constructor is factored. V1 bytes, HKDF inputs, AAD, error mapping, randomness order/count and rewrap semantics unchanged; no public API or format change. Tests: new crypto/tests/fixed_buffers.rs (fixed wrap equals encrypt_bytes output and both unwrap paths recover the key; every single-byte change of the 48 wrapper bytes and mismatched key/nonce/AAD fail with AuthenticationFailed); all 45 at-rest lib tests, public_api tests and doctests pass; node generate-envelope-v1.mjs --check matches. Allocation probe (throwaway, outside repo, counting GlobalAlloc, release and debug identical, setup excluded, key IDs 'old'/'new', test row context): seal before 6 allocs [83 payload AAD, body, 64 HKDF info, 102 wrapper AAD, 48 wrapped key, 3 key ID] -> after 5 (48 removed); open empty before 4 [64,102,32,83] -> after 3; open 64B/1KiB before 5 -> after 4 (32-byte unwrap buffer removed); rewrap_envelope and rewrap same-key before 4 [64,102,32,3] -> after 3; changed-key before 7 [64,102,32,64,102,48,3] -> after 5. Remaining allocations are HKDF info, wrapper/payload AAD, key-ID copy and owned body/plaintext, as scoped. Release timings (two runs, 5 rounds x 50,000): seal empty 2643/3282 -> 2596/2605 ns; seal 64B 2679/2673 -> 2645/2664; open empty 1265/1528 -> 1211/1196; open 64B 1310/1315 -> 1297/1283; same-key rewrap_envelope 924/1136 -> 883/878 (empty), 909/912 -> 880/879 (64B); changed-key 2242/2241 -> 2201/2282 (empty), 2239/2231 -> 2196/2206 (64B). Differences are 0-5 percent with run-to-run noise of the same size; no speedup is claimed. Verification: bash scripts/verify.sh exit 0 on the pinned 1.98.1 toolchain (fmt, file budget, four Clippy configurations, six test-matrix parts with 3717 tests passed / 0 failed / 374 ignored, rustdoc, all HTTP smoke profiles). MSRV 1.94.0 left to CI. Docs: crates/batter-at-rest/README.md allocation sentence, docs/status.md new row, docs/testing.md paragraph, CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry.

fields.description: Deferred observation from batter-esla (2026-10-15), not a review finding. crates/batter-at-rest/src/crypto.rs derive_wrapping_key allocates its HKDF info buffer with Vec::with_capacity(64) but writes 10 + namespace + purpose bytes (HKDF magic, version and role bytes, and two length-prefixed label frames). Context labels may each be up to MAX_CONTEXT_LABEL_BYTES (64), so a namespace plus purpose longer than 54 bytes combined reallocates the Zeroizing buffer once per seal, open and rewrap. Out of batter-esla's scope by its recorded decision that AAD and HKDF buffers remain.
fields.acceptance_criteria: derive_wrapping_key sizes the info buffer from the actual label lengths so no reallocation occurs for any valid context; HKDF inputs and derived keys are byte-identical (Node fixture and RFC 5869 tests pass unchanged); a unit test or throwaway probe shows no growth for maximum-length labels; scripts/verify.sh passes on the pinned toolchain.

fields.description:
## Problem

`crates/batter-sqlx/Cargo.toml` declares the optional test-support dependency
`postgres-test-harness = { version = "0.2.0", git = ..., rev = "3d525e6fc5745ce2e2437c7997de5cccdecff4ac" }`
and `examples/reference-service` pins the same Git revision. On publication Cargo
strips the Git source and dependents resolve registry 0.2.0. The published 0.2.0
crate (SHA-256 ae16463f0ea9790d102559acc5dda876b3dfe577ed8d338b2b8023cc7fdf2456) was
compared with the pinned revision on 2026-10-17: `src/harness.rs` and
`src/fingerprint.rs` differ by 292 lines; the revision is eight commits past 0.2.0
and adds `DatabaseTemplate::derive`, derived fingerprints and the fix "retain
template sources through detached copy workers". Batter uses only items that exist
in 0.2.0, so a published `batter-sqlx` compiles, but its test-support feature would
run harness behavior that local evidence never executed. `cargo deny check sources`
fails on the Git source.

## Resolution

Owner action in the harness repository: publish the pinned revision (or a reviewed
successor) as a new registry version. Then change both declarations to a registry
version with no `git`/`rev` keys and regenerate `Cargo.lock` with Cargo.

Evidence: docs/evidence/publication-dossier-2026-10-17.md, section "Harness source mismatch".
fields.acceptance_criteria: crates/batter-sqlx/Cargo.toml declares postgres-test-harness by registry version only, at a version whose published source matches the previously pinned revision; cargo deny sources passes; the reference example declares the same version; bash scripts/verify.sh passes on Rust 1.98.1.

fields.description:
SECURITY.md requires an owner-controlled private vulnerability reporting channel
before publication and forbids inventing a maintainer contact. On 2026-10-17 the
GitHub API returned `{"enabled": false}` for the repository, unchanged since the
2026-09-22 publication-preparation comment on `batter-ddc`.

Owner action, one time, from an account with admin rights on the repository:

    gh api -X PUT repos/bpcakes/batter/private-vulnerability-reporting

or Settings > Code security > Private vulnerability reporting > Enable. No
maintainer email address is to be added to SECURITY.md.

Evidence: docs/evidence/publication-dossier-2026-10-17.md, gate table.
fields.acceptance_criteria: GET /repos/bpcakes/batter/private-vulnerability-reporting returns enabled: true; the Security tab shows the report form; the result is recorded here and in the dossier gate table.

fields.description:
RUSTSEC-2026-0205 (unsound): `scc` 2.4.0 `Array::insert` violates exception
safety when a caller-supplied comparison function panics. Patched in scc 3.8.4.
The workspace reaches scc only through `metrics-exporter-otel` 0.3.1, used by
`batter-otlp`, and that crate requires `scc ^2.1`, so no lock update can resolve
it. Batter's exporter supplies no comparison function, but that is an upstream
dependency decision, not a local proof.

Watch for a `metrics-exporter-otel` release that moves to scc 3.x, then update the
locked graph with Cargo and run bash scripts/verify.sh. Do not vendor or fork.

Evidence: docs/evidence/publication-dossier-2026-10-17.md, section "Advisories".
fields.acceptance_criteria: cargo audit reports no unsound warning for scc, or the retained warning is recorded with the upstream issue link and a dated re-check; no local fork of metrics-exporter-otel.
